title: Ranked slot reclamation: conditional κ = 4.764513337e-5
body:
This refines PR #58's conditional witness by changing the order in which its compiler tries retired auxiliary slots:

$$
T(n)=O\left(n(\log n)^{1-\kappa}\right),\qquad
\kappa=\frac{4764513337}{10^{14}}=4.764513337\times10^{-5}>2^{-15}.
$$

The exponent saving is **0.290011% above #58** (`475073569/10^13`). The exact bit saving is `2382370177/50000000000000`. The inherited analytic and fixed finite-alphabet multitape hypotheses remain unchanged.

## Change

Try retired slots in **descending current frame rank**, breaking ties by slot ID. The previous order was ascending slot ID. The scalar graph, frame family, matching algorithm, legality checks, and same-frame synthesis are unchanged.

A slot can be reused only in a containing frame. Trying larger frames first is intended to preserve smaller-frame slots for later regions. This is a search heuristic. Correctness still follows from the checked containment and span conditions, explicitly paid clearing XORs, and the complete compute/scatter/uncompute word on arbitrary dirty state.

| Quantity | PR #58 | This PR |
|---|---:|---:|
| h=23 auxiliary roles | 30,790 | **30,688** |
| h=25 auxiliary roles | 40,446 | **40,338** |
| Physical wires W | 150,593,466 | **150,167,598** |

The actual fixed-basis block profiles give rank **86,344,521,950**, deficit **1,846,900**, and maximum child width **529**. All 4,073,300 data pairs, copied centers, paid endpoints, complex branch, and assembly interfaces remain charged. The original shared compiler remains byte-identical; a dedicated compiler module isolates this single scheduling change.

## Verification

Independent replay of both selected words passes every source, target, and dirty basis vector in both orientations, reconstructs every frame transition from literal XOR incidences, and confirms exact fixed-I+J profiles with zero CRT disagreements. Exact rational checks prove all **47 assembly inequalities and seven margins**, reject both next grid points, and exclude PR #58's complete network at the new bit saving. The pinned #58 certificate is retained for comparison.

The bounded search compared seven candidates per axis and all 49 pairings. This is not a global optimality claim. Fresh packaged regeneration passes both axes, every profile, and ten focused rejection/replay tests. Independent audit passes all 30 adversarial controls and all 51 source pins. The expanded current-main `make verify` completed successfully: **429 integrated tests, 28 restored research audits, and all 20 historical patch checks**, with no generated-file drift. An independent review verified the upstream integration, source closure, unchanged mathematics, and completed receipt.

```sh
make joint-dual-verify
make verify
```

Tested current-main construction: `94c97bd367782c9530bee7c17d229bd4b1e0a2b7`, incorporating main `d55bcd62ceb8f322bcf311a5a66e94c3ac7724f0` and PR #58 head `be5d3e6e39ad9a11372f168e37466af412e51e53`. The [proof](https://github.com/chafreaky/integer-mult-bounds/blob/94c97bd367782c9530bee7c17d229bd4b1e0a2b7/research/joint-dual/PROOF.md) and [exact certificate](https://github.com/chafreaky/integer-mult-bounds/blob/94c97bd367782c9530bee7c17d229bd4b1e0a2b7/certificates/joint-dual-kappa.json) are pinned to that tested construction; the [completed verification receipt](https://github.com/chafreaky/integer-mult-bounds/blob/21a121960644b8c6fdf9c06fe39dea1944dd2231/certificates/joint-dual-repository-validation.json) records the expanded run and preserves the earlier complete construction verification. The upstream merge preserves the original words, profiles, and exact arithmetic, and updates the Makefile/README source pins. This branch builds on PR #58. The finite certificate does not prove the inherited all-size framed-word transfer, residual compiler, finite-alphabet tape layout, analytic, routing, prime-selection, or recovery obligations.

Published-head CI: **20/20 checks passed** on `21a121960644b8c6fdf9c06fe39dea1944dd2231` across Python 3.11, 3.13, 3.14 and the retained formal packages. The formal jobs cover their existing packages; they do not establish a new full formal multiplication theorem.
